title: Why You Should NEVER Write a Name in Red Ink in Korea
description: Grabbed a red pen to write your Korean friend's name? Big mistake. Here's the surprisingly heavy reason why. What's a color rule in YOUR culture? Share below!

sections.narration: Imagine you borrow a red pen and casually write your Korean friend's name on a sticky note.
sections.visual_notes: Centered: boy writing with red pen on yellow note, warm desk scene

sections.narration: They see it, and their face just drops — like you said something really heavy.
sections.visual_notes: Centered: boy holding note, friend looking startled, warm classroom

sections.narration: They grab the note and crumple it up immediately, no questions asked.
sections.visual_notes: Centered: boy confused, friend crumpling paper, warm indoor lighting

sections.narration: So here's the deal — in Korea, red ink was traditionally used to record names of the deceased.
sections.visual_notes: Centered: boy looking at old document with red characters, warm sepia tone

sections.narration: Official records would write a person's name in red after they had passed away.
sections.visual_notes: Centered: boy beside old registry book, red text visible, warm archive

sections.narration: And it gets weirder — writing a living person's name in red is like wishing them gone.
sections.visual_notes: Centered: boy putting down red pen, picking up blue pen, warm desk

sections.narration: But here's the thing — red ink is totally fine for stamps and seals in Korea.
sections.visual_notes: Centered: boy pressing red stamp on document, official seal, warm office

sections.narration: It's specifically writing someone's personal name in red that crosses the line.
sections.visual_notes: Centered: boy with name tag, red X over red pen, blue check over blue pen

sections.narration: So THAT'S why your friend freaked out — you basically wrote a really bad omen.
sections.visual_notes: Centered: boy with lightbulb, red pen crossed out, warm background

sections.narration: Just grab a blue or black pen and everything stays perfectly chill.
sections.visual_notes: Centered: boy writing happily with blue pen, friend smiling, warm room

sections.narration: Next time you reach for a red pen, maybe think twice about what you're writing.
sections.visual_notes: Centered: boy choosing between pens, picking blue, warm desk scene
Centered: boy giving thumbs up, warm earth-toned background, simple
